problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.description:
Given an integer array `nums` sorted in **non-decreasing order**, remove the duplicates **in-place** such that each unique element appears only **once**. The relative order of the elements should be kept the same. Then return the number of unique elements in `nums`.

Expected output: the deduplicated prefix array (the test runner verifies `k = len(expected)` and `nums[:k] == expected`).
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
problems.approach_brute: Copy unique elements to a new array, then back. O(N) time and space.
problems.approach_optimal: Slow/fast two pointers. Slow tracks where the next unique should land; fast scans forward. When `nums[fast] != nums[slow]`, advance slow and copy. Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Remove Element
problems.description:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `val`, remove all occurrences of `val` in `nums` **in-place**. The order of the elements may be changed. Then return the number of elements in `nums` which are not equal to `val`.

Expected output: the **sorted** prefix of remaining elements.
problems.approach_brute: Build a new array excluding val. O(N) time and space.
problems.approach_optimal: Slow/fast pointers. Slow = next write position. Fast scans; when nums[fast] != val, write to nums[slow] and slow++. Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Move Zeroes
problems.description:
Given an integer array `nums`, move all `0`'s to the end of it while maintaining the **relative order** of the non-zero elements.

**Note** that you must do this **in-place** without making a copy of the array.
problems.approach_brute: Build a new array and copy back. O(N) extra space.
problems.approach_optimal: Slow/fast: slow tracks where next non-zero lands; fast scans. When `nums[fast] != 0`, swap with `nums[slow]` and slow++. Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Linked List Cycle
problems.description:
Given `head`, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it.

There is a cycle in a linked list if there is some node in the list that can be reached again by continuously following the `next` pointer.

Return `true` if there is a cycle in the linked list. Otherwise, return `false`.

The input is given as `{head: number[], pos: number}` where `pos` is the index where the tail's `next` connects (or `-1` for no cycle), and both are passed to your function.
constraints: pos is -1 or a valid index in the linked list
problems.approach_brute: Hash set of visited nodes. O(N) time and space.
problems.approach_optimal: Floyd's tortoise and hare. Slow advances 1 step, fast advances 2 steps. They meet iff a cycle exists. Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Linked List Cycle II
problems.description:
Given the `head` of a linked list, return the **node where the cycle begins**. If there is no cycle, return `null`.

The input is given as `{head: number[], pos: number}` where `pos` is the index where the tail's `next` connects (or `-1` for no cycle), and both are passed to your function.

Expected output: the index of the cycle-start node, or `-1` if no cycle.
constraints: pos is -1 or a valid index
problems.approach_brute: Hash set of visited nodes; first repeat is the cycle start. O(N) time and space.
problems.approach_optimal: Floyd's tortoise and hare. After they meet, reset one pointer to head and advance both one step at a time; they meet again at the cycle start. The math: distance from head to cycle-start = distance from meeting-point to cycle-start (mod cycle length). Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Middle of the Linked List
problems.description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list, return the **middle node** of the linked list.

If there are two middle nodes, return the **second middle** node.

Expected output: the list of values from the middle node to the tail.
problems.approach_brute: Count length, then iterate to length/2. Two passes.
problems.approach_optimal: Slow/fast pointers. Fast advances 2 steps per slow's 1. When fast reaches end, slow is at middle. One pass. Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
problems.description:
Given the `head` of a linked list, remove the n-th node from the end of the list and return its head.

Expected output: the modified list as an array of values.
problems.approach_brute: Two passes: count length, then remove (length - n)-th node from front.
problems.approach_optimal: Single pass with two pointers separated by n+1 nodes (using a dummy). Advance both until the leading pointer reaches null; the trailing one is at the predecessor of the node to remove. Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Happy Number
problems.description:
Write an algorithm to determine if a number `n` is happy.

A **happy number** is a number defined by the following process:

- Starting with any positive integer, replace the number by the sum of the squares of its digits.
- Repeat the process until the number equals `1` (where it will stay), or it loops endlessly in a cycle which does not include `1`.
- Those numbers for which this process **ends in 1** are happy.

Return `true` if `n` is a happy number, and `false` if not.
problems.approach_brute: Hash set of seen values; if `1` is reached → happy, if a value repeats → not happy. O(log n · iterations) time, O(iterations) space.
problems.approach_optimal: Floyd's cycle detection on the digit-square-sum function. Slow advances one step, fast advances two. They meet at 1 (happy) or in the non-happy cycle. Time O(log n · iterations), space O(1).

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
problems.description:
Given an integer array `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, remove some duplicates **in-place** such that each unique element appears **at most twice**. The relative order of the elements should be kept the same.

Return the new prefix as the modified array (test driver compares `nums[:k]` with expected).
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
problems.approach_brute: Build a new array enforcing the at-most-twice rule. O(N) extra space.
problems.approach_optimal: Slow/fast pointers. Allow nums[fast] into nums[slow] iff slow < 2 OR nums[fast] != nums[slow-2]. Advance slow accordingly. Generalizes to 'at most K' by checking nums[fast] != nums[slow-K]. Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Find the Duplicate Number
problems.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` containing `n + 1` integers where each integer is in the range `[1, n]` inclusive.

There is only **one repeated number** in `nums`, return the repeated number.

You must solve the problem **without modifying** the array `nums` and uses only **constant extra space**.
constraints: Exactly one duplicate, may appear more than once
edge_cases: Already sorted with last element duplicating an earlier value
problems.approach_brute: Sort and scan, or hash set. O(N log N) or O(N) time / O(N) space.
problems.approach_optimal: Treat indices as a functional graph: i → nums[i]. Since one value repeats, the graph has a cycle. Apply Floyd's cycle detection — slow/fast pointers; meeting point + reset trick locates the duplicate. Time O(N), space O(1).

problems.title: Partition Labels
problems.description:
You are given a string `s`. We want to partition the string into as **many parts as possible** so that **each letter appears in at most one part**.

Note that the partition is done so that after concatenating all the parts in order, the resultant string should be `s`.

Return a list of integers representing the **size of these parts**.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
edge_cases: One part covers the whole string
problems.approach_brute: Greedy with re-scanning to find boundaries. O(N^2).
problems.approach_optimal: Precompute the last occurrence of every letter. Then sweep: maintain current partition's required end as the maximum of last-occurrence of every letter encountered so far. When the current index reaches that end, close the partition. Time O(N), space O(σ).

problems.title: String Compression
problems.description:
Given an array of characters `chars`, compress it using the following algorithm:

Begin with an empty string `s`. For each group of **consecutive repeating characters** in `chars`:
- If the group's length is `1`, append the character to `s`.
- Otherwise, append the character followed by the group's length.

The compressed string `s` should not be returned separately, but instead, be stored **in the input character array `chars`**. Note that group lengths that are `10` or longer will be split into multiple characters in `chars`.

After you are done modifying the input array, return the new length of the array.

Expected output: the modified prefix array.
constraints: chars[i] is a lowercase English letter, uppercase English letter, digit, or symbol
problems.approach_brute: Build a fresh compressed string then copy back. O(N) extra space.
problems.approach_optimal: Two pointers: read pointer scans groups; write pointer emits compressed output in-place. After identifying each group, write the character; if count > 1, write the digits. Time O(N), space O(1).
